newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks end 0.5 percent higher.
newsitem.headline: French stocks end 0.5 percent higher.

text.p: French stocks finished higher on Monday, underpinned by gains on Wall Street and leading European bourses, brokers said. Block trades ahead of Tuesday's expiry of futures and options accounted for much of the activity.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index finished up 11.68 points, or 0.51 percent, at 2,318.63. The CAC-40 futures contract rose 13.50 points to 2,319.
Volume was 4.3 billion francs, inflated by block trades in many of the CAC-40 issues.
* LVMH rose 2.32 percent to 1,455 francs on reports of record champagne sales this year, in volume terms.
The newspaper Les Echos said more than 250 million bottles of champagne would be sold this year, breaking the previous record of 249 million set in 1989. LVMH is the top seller.

* Renault shares rose 1.44 percent to 112.60 francs after a rollercoaster session. Company officials were unavailable to comment on remarks by the managing director of Finnish vehicle group Sisu Oy that Renault may buy its trucks business.
Shares in carmaker PSA Peugeot Citroen, which have performed much better than Renault this year, finished down 1.35 percent at 584 francs.
* Bis shares were suspended on Monday after the death of chairman and founder Laurent Negro whose family holds more than 50 percent of the temporary workers' firm's capital.

Analysts said his death raises prospects for Bis to take part in an industry consolidation marked by the merger of Ecco and Adia. They said Manpower might be a possible suitor. "The founder's death will arouse speculation about the company and shareholder structure," one analyst said.
* Accor rose 2.24 percent to 638 francs. The newspaper Les Echos said the town council of Dax was set to finalise an agreement with Accor on its thermal baths.
* Compagnie Bancaire finished up 3.32 percent at 622 francs. Operators said the share had been lagging recently.
* For the year to date, the CAC index is up 23.86 percent. Analysts see less scope for gains next year, with many expecting the index to go no higher than 2,450 during 1997.
